terradish: Fast Gradient-Based Optimization of Resistance Surfaces

Source: R/terradish-package.R
terradish-package.Rd

Estimates landscape conductance surfaces from genetic data by maximum likelihood on a raster graph. It fits log-linear conductance models and can optionally estimate each covariate's Gaussian smoothing scale and spline shape. Models fit pairwise genetic distances through the MLPE likelihood, or allele-frequency covariance and squared distances derived from it through a Wishart likelihood on site contrasts. Both families accept the same pairwise environmental covariates alongside resistance. Exact sparse Cholesky and algebraic multigrid solvers handle large rasters; fixed-domain spatial cross-validation compares conductance formulas.

Details

Where to start. conductance_surface builds the graph, terradish fits the model, and the methods documented in terradish_methods (summary(), coef(), plot(), anova()) read the result. Conductance parameters are on the log scale, so exp(coef(fit)) is the multiplicative change in conductance per unit of a covariate. These coefficients describe conditional associations within the fitted graph and candidate set. They do not, by themselves, identify causal mechanisms, absolute migration or dispersal rates, or habitat suitability. For Wishart models, the user-supplied effective degrees of freedom, nu, sets inferential precision. Using the SNP count substantially overstated information in the package's forward-time validation experiments. Report sensitivity across plausible values with terradish_rescale_nu.

Main components.

Conductance models

loglinear_conductance (the default), smooth_loglinear_conductance for spline responses, and gaussian_smoothed_loglinear_conductance for estimating a covariate's Gaussian raster-smoothing scale inside the model.

Measurement models

leastsquares and mlpe for a genetic distance matrix; generalized_wishart and wishart_covariance for a Wishart likelihood, which need the effective degrees of freedom nu; check_distance_response to verify a generalized-Wishart squared-distance response; mlpe_covariates and wishart_covariates to add isolation-by-environment terms.

Pairwise inputs and inference

pairwise_covariates combines geographic distances and environmental differences; terradish_ibe_ratio expresses their fitted effects in resistance-distance units. terradish_inference provides covariance matrices and confidence intervals, and gaussian_scale_profile profiles smoothing-scale uncertainty.

Comparison and diagnostics

aic_table, terradish_cv_folds, terradish_grid, and terradish_assess_settings, a speed probe for solver and optimizer settings. It does not establish statistical validity.

Preparation and design

scale_covariates, crop_to_focal_buffer, simulate_covariance_response, and covariance_response_power support reproducible inputs and model-based study design. slim_terradish reduces stored fit size when later prediction is unnecessary.

Parameter names and their scales. Several names recur with different meanings. Read each one on the scale of the model that reports it.

theta

Conductance parameters, returned by coef(). Log-linear and spline coefficients are on the log-conductance scale, so exp(theta) is a conductance multiplier per unit of the covariate. Gaussian sigma.<layer> entries of theta are smoothing scales in map units.

phi

Nuisance parameters of the measurement model, reported by summary(). Their names and scales depend on the model: alpha, beta, tau, rho, sigma, and environmental coefficients.

tau

In mlpe and leastsquares, the log residual precision: the residual variance is exp(-tau). In wishart_covariance, generalized_wishart, and simulate_covariance_response, the nonnegative multiplier on the graph covariance, on its natural scale.

sigma

In fitted Wishart models, the log nugget variance: the nugget is exp(sigma). In simulate_covariance_response and covariance_response_power, the nugget variance itself, on its natural scale. In gaussian_smoothed_loglinear_conductance, a Gaussian smoothing scale in map units (sigma.<layer>). In HagerZhangControl, a line-search constant unrelated to any model.

rho

In mlpe, the shared-site correlation on a logit scale: the correlation is plogis(rho) / 2, between 0 and 0.5. rho_start in mlpe_covariates is on the natural scale. In HagerZhangControl, an unrelated line-search constant.

nu

Effective Wishart degrees of freedom, supplied by the user and never estimated. It scales the log-likelihood, so standard errors scale as 1 / sqrt(nu) while point estimates do not change. It is not the marker count. Unused by the distance models.

alpha, beta

In the distance models, the intercept and the slope of genetic distance on resistance distance, in the units of the response.

lambda_<covariate>

In wishart_covariates, a nonnegative weight on an environmental covariance kernel.

Moving from radish. The original radish* function names still work but are deprecated; see radish_compatibility.

Experimental features. Directed and hierarchical models, site-specific drift terms, selected-pair likelihoods, and other research prototypes remain on the experimental branch. Their identifiability and validation limits are described in that branch's EXPERIMENTAL.md. Install it explicitly with remotes::install_github("wpeterman/terradish@experimental").

Vignettes. Start with vignette("v01-getting-started", package = "terradish"), or with vignette("v03-mlpe-pairwise-distance", package = "terradish") if your data are a pairwise genetic distance matrix. The others cover model comparison, joint isolation by environment and resistance, the covariance-based Wishart workflow, spline conductance, scale optimization, large landscapes, and simulation-based study design. List them all with browseVignettes("terradish").

Worked examples

vignette("v12-data-generation", package = "terradish"), vignette("v01-getting-started", package = "terradish"), vignette("v09-individual-salamanders", package = "terradish"), vignette("v03-mlpe-pairwise-distance", package = "terradish").
